slides.stem: The experiment failed ______ the team learned more from it than they expected.
slides.prompt: Most students pick the same wrong answer. Comment yours.

slides.title: B — the semicolon
slides.body: Both sides are complete sentences, and a comma alone can't hold two apart — that's the comma splice. "However" between commas doesn't fix it, and C fuses the sentences with nothing at all.

slides.title: The 10-second punctuation check
slides.body: Cover the punctuation and read each side alone. Two complete sentences? You need a period, a semicolon, or a comma *with* and/but/so. A comma by itself is never enough — no matter what word comes after it.
